messages.subject: Re: Issue 88 in stan: stan_rdump patch
parts:
Comment #1 on issue 88 by guoj...@gmail.com: stan_rdump patch
http://code.google.com/p/stan/issues/detail?id=88

Thanks.

I do not think this is a defect. It is at most an enhancement.

If a user really want a vector of length 1 to be consider for say "real
y[1]", the correct way now is to dump a variable y with dim = c(1) in R
(that is, "array(y, dim = 1)").

I guess I will add the optional argument quiet later. I do not know how
many people would like that.

Comment #2 on issue 88 by ca...@alias-i.com: stan_rdump patch
http://code.google.com/p/stan/issues/detail?id=88

I think we should do this for the dump reader. I'm a little reluctant to
drop it in right now before our next release, but I'll get it into the next
release.

The problem is with how R writes its output. If I write x = c(3) in R and
then dump(c('x')), it just writes out x <- 3.

Jiqiang's technically right in the sense that it's not a bug with respect
to the current spec of our command-line dump reader.

The question is how R dumps an array of length 1 and then how Stan could
read it in. So I think this is something to patch on the command-line dump
reader, not in RStan.

messages.author: 5b11633594333711
messages.subject: Re: Issue 88 in stan: stan_rdump patch
parts:
Comment #3 on issue 88 by ca...@alias-i.com: stan_rdump patch
http://code.google.com/p/stan/issues/detail?id=88

The submitted path (from Jeffrey Arnold) is trying to fix the RStan side,
so that it writes output that Stan can read. I think that's a reasonable
idea -- the cleaner we can make the output, the better.

But the real issue is that the dump reader in Stan (not in RStan) needs to
be made more robust. I wrote it originally not realizing the can of works
I was opening because R is so quirky with how it interconverts and writes
scalars and arrays/vectors of size 1, which to me, look like completely
different beasts.

The problem is in the dump reader, but I didn't know how to fix that, so I fixed what could.  It is a serious enough problem for me that I use my own dump writer because there are models that I run that otherwise I would need to write separate models for every time a vector has a length of 1.

messages.subject: Re: Issue 88 in stan: stan_rdump patch
parts:
Comment #4 on issue 88 by guoj...@gmail.com: stan_rdump patch
http://code.google.com/p/stan/issues/detail?id=88

I guess I am not still sure about the issue here. As R does not treat the
following differently:

a <- 3

a <- c(3)

So I think in this case, we treat the above "a" in any case as a scalar is
a good choice, which also make the code and data more portable. I can
image people would write "real y[1]" in their code sometimes. In this
case, its input from R should be

y <- array(3, dim = 1).

This is a bit more code but it can serve as a way to discourage not to use
an array of length 1.

messages.author: 5b11633594333711
messages.subject: Re: Issue 88 in stan: stan_rdump patch
parts:
Comment #5 on issue 88 by jeffrey....@gmail.com: stan_rdump patch
http://code.google.com/p/stan/issues/detail?id=88

Sorry that it was tagged as a defect, there is no enhancement template.

I hadn't thought about using array. That is a much cleaner hack, and now I
don't see the need for my patch after being made aware of this work around.

But is is still a hack, and I think this should be fixed in the dump
reader. For one, it is not obvious; I'm fairly proficient with R and using
array in this case didn't occur to me. It is also inconsistent with the
other behavior of the dump reader. For vectors, 1d arrays and row_vectors,
will read vectors in which there is no dimension attribute. That only
chokes in the case when the length of the vector/array is 1.

I share your annoyance this is all because R has no concept of scalars. I
wonder if there is an alternative to using R dumps; maybe something like
protobuf.

This isn't about discouraging arrays of length 1. These instances arise
when the same model applies to cases with n>=1, the n isn't known until
run-time, and it wouldn't make sense to write a separate model for just the
n=1 case. For example, I have factor model code, in which there are several
vectors of length equal to the number of factors; when there is 1 factor
they have length 1. This issue arises often enough that I wrote my own dump
function to handle it
(https://github.com/jrnold/StanExtras/blob/master/R/write_stan.R).
